blocks.text: 发生了什么
Cloudflare 的部署配置的上下文长度为 1,048,576 个 token，但其预填充 KV 缓存池只能容纳 681,280 个 token。因此，一个请求可能符合配置的上下文窗口，却超出可用于处理它的内存。

blocks.text: 背景
在 PD 分离式服务中，prefill 阶段和 decode 阶段运行在独立的引擎上，每个请求的 KVCache 必须从 prefill 引擎迁移到 decode 引擎的内存池中。为了性能，这一传输是异步的。Mooncake、NIXL 或 MORI 等传输引擎将其作为单边 RDMA WRITE 操作发出，在 prefill 计算仍在进行时，将 KVCache 分块流式写入预先保留的目标槽位。

inlines.text: 在 PD 分离式服务中，prefill 阶段和 decode 阶段运行在独立的引擎上，每个请求的 KVCache 必须从 prefill 引擎迁移到 decode 引擎的内存池中。为了性能，这一传输是异步的。Mooncake、NIXL 或 MORI 等传输引擎将其作为单边 RDMA WRITE 操作发出，在 prefill 计算仍在进行时，将 KVCache 分块流式写入预先保留的目标槽位。

blocks.text: 由于传输是异步的，一个请求可能在其部分写入仍在进行中时终止。此时 prefill 可以丢弃仍在其软件队列中等待的分块，但无法停止已经发往目标的写入，例如当时正在传输中的分块。在早期的实现中，当请求在传输中途终止（客户端断开连接、超时、传输故障）时，decode 会在终止时将其目标槽位归还给分配器，而不等待此类写入完成。如果分配器在该写入落地之前重新分配了这些槽位，已终止请求的 KVCache 就会落入另一个请求的 KVCache 中。在典型工作负载下，这种损坏很少发生，尽管长上下文会使其可能性大大增加（见下文事实 4）。每次发生都是静默的。传输报告成功，没有任何组件抛出异常或记录错误。单个被污染的槽位就会毁掉整个生成过程，因为注意力机制会读取每一个位置。

blocks.text: 该故障分为四步：

inlines.text: 客户端断开连接、准入拒绝或传输故障导致请求 A 在传输中途中止，此时至少有一个已发出的写入尚未落地。
Decode 在中止时释放 A 的 KVCache 槽位。分配器将其标记为空闲，而远程写入器仍在向其写入。
分配器将这些槽位交给受害请求 B。
A 已发出的写入落入 B 的 KVCache 中，B 使用外来的键和值进行解码，且没有任何错误。

blocks.text: 这些步骤适用于任何使用异步 DMA（推送或拉取）在引擎之间迁移 KVCache 的 PD 实现，因为每个实现都必须决定槽位何时空闲。我们在 SGLang 中诊断并修复了这一类问题。

blocks.text: 1. 分配器可以在写入仍在进行中时将槽位标记为空闲。在 PD 分离中，decode 引擎为每个传入请求预先保留目标 KVCache 槽位，其分配器将它们跟踪为已分配或空闲。但“空闲”还有第二个隐藏条件：只有当没有远程写入器仍能触及该槽位时，该槽位才可以安全复用。这一类 bug 正源于这两个定义之间的差距。每一个都是分布式 use-after-free，其中悬空指针是位于另一台机器 NIC 队列中的写请求。修复方案使第二个条件变得显式、可观测且有界。

blocks.text: 2. 已启动的 RDMA 工作无法取消，push 和 pull 都是如此。 SGLang 的 KVCache 传输是基于 push 的 [3]。Prefill 将 KVCache 写入 decode 的内存，因为 prefill 知道它产生每个 chunk 的时刻，并且可以逐 chunk 地将传输与正在进行的计算重叠。在 NIC 及以下层面，若不损害可用性，取消很难实现。RDMA API 没有可以取消已提交到 NIC 队列对的单个工作请求的调用。Python 无法在调用中途中断传输引擎的阻塞式 C++ 调用（例如 Mooncake 的 batch_transfer_sync）。如果该调用超时，其工作请求会保持已提交状态且没有完成记账，因此这些写入可能在未知的稍后时间落地。单边 RDMA WRITE 绕过接收方 CPU，因此 decode 不会收到每次写入的信号以供其等待。NIC 还按数据包放置数据：一次在传输中途被中断的写入仍会在目标端留下部分写入的前缀，因此即使看起来像取消的路径也可能改变目标内存。

blocks.text: 3. 完整的存活处理始于路由器，但不能止于路由器。 只有当 P/D 对的两半都得知中止时，中止才是安全的。设计良好的 PD 路由器会成对取消，因此任何一方都不会为一个永远不会到来的对端等待 300 秒超时。在 sgl-router 中，#41612 在 #39461 的断连即中止机制之上构建了 PD 配对。该对共享一个由路由器生成的请求 id。客户端断连会中止 decode，prefill 失败会丢弃 decode 请求，从而使引擎中止它，而 prefill 通过 decode 引擎侧的 ABORT 通知得知中止。sgl-model-gateway 将同样两个事件配对（#19524 用于断连，#29017 用于 prefill 失败）。在该引擎侧通知出现之前，只中止一侧的路由器必然导致竞态：decode 释放其槽位，而从未被告知的 prefill 继续推送。即使完美的路由器也只能缩小窗口。中止会异步到达 prefill，经过一些调度和网络延迟，而传输引擎已经启动的任何内容（进行中的 C++ 调用、已提交的工作请求）都会继续。路由器决定谁死亡（中止编排），引擎决定内存何时安全（排空正确性）。

#43719 于 2026 年 10 月 12 日合并，关闭了 Mooncake drain ack 中的一条提前释放路径。在此之前，如果提交的 Mooncake 发送返回错误，prefill 会将房间标记为失败，但一旦 decode 的 ABORT 到达，仍会将其确认为已排空。来自 batch_transfer_sync 的错误并不意味着写入已停止：超时后，切片会继续重试；批次失败后，其他任务仍可能在进行中。Decode 在该确认后释放了槽位，而残留的写入可能落入另一个请求的 KVCache。#43719 对任何 KVCache、状态或 aux 发送失败的房间暂不发送 drain ack，因此 decode 会保留槽位直到其释放超时。现在每次发送失败都会带来这一保留代价，直到 Mooncake 能够报告失败的批次是否已排空。#43719 已在 main 上，将在 v0.5.22 中发布。

blocks.text: 准入修复

准入控制从路由器开始。PD 路由器将每个请求同时发送给一个 prefill worker 和一个 decode worker，而 decode 在没有 prefill 的 KVCache 时无法生成 token。如果 prefill 拒绝或使请求失败，decode 这一半过去会在持有 decode 槽位的同时等待其 300 秒超时，因此一波 prefill 失败可能同时占住许多 decode 槽位。sgl-model-gateway 中的 #29017 和 sgl-router 中的 #41612 现在会在 prefill 返回错误时立即丢弃 decode 请求，decode 引擎会在数秒内中止它。

blocks.text: PD校验和

#39500于2026年9月16日合并，为传输的KVCache增加了可选的完整性检查，默认关闭。Prefill在GPU上对连续区域以及带索引的KVCache和状态页计算Adler-32校验和，并随最后一个chunk发送。Decode在提交传输时记录它，并在请求加入运行批次之前用其检查接收到的KVCache，因此能捕获在该时间点之前到达的延迟写入；保持机制会阻止后续写入进入被复用的槽位。Decode在撤回期间保留校验和。不匹配会中止请求并递增传输失败计数器；在CI中，不匹配会抛出错误。健康检查请求跳过该检查。

绝不要释放异步引擎可能仍会访问的槽位。

让每一种降级都延长保持时间。

blocks.text: What happened

Cloudflare’s deployment had a configured context length of 1,048,576 tokens, but its prefill KV cache pool could hold 681,280 tokens. A request could therefore fit the configured context window while exceeding the memory available to process it.

blocks.text: In SGLang’s disaggregated prefill/decode path, a request marked for rejection could still proceed through the handoff. Decode could then read cache pages that had not been populated for that request. The configuration mismatch made the rejection path reachable. The admission fix described below ensures that a rejected request returns an error before entering the disaggregated handoff. It complements deployment checks that compare pool capacity with the configured context length.

blocks.text: Background

In PD-disaggregated serving, the prefill and decode phases run on separate engines, and each request’s KVCache must move from the prefill engine into the decode engine’s memory pool. For performance, this transfer is asynchronous. Transfer engines such as Mooncake, NIXL, or MORI issue it as one-sided RDMA WRITE operations that stream KVCache chunks into pre-reserved destination slots while prefill computation is still in progress.

For performance, this transfer is asynchronous. blocks.text: Because the transfer is asynchronous, a request can die while some of its writes are in flight. Prefill can then drop the chunks still waiting in its software queues, but it cannot stop a write it has launched toward the destination, such as the chunk in progress at that moment. In earlier implementations, when a request terminated mid-transfer (a client disconnect, a timeout, a transport fault), decode returned its destination slots to the allocator at termination, without waiting for such a write to finish. If the allocator reassigned the slots before the write landed, the dead request’s KVCache landed in another request’s KVCache. In typical workloads the corruption was rare, although long contexts make it far more likely (see fact 4 below). Each occurrence was silent. The transfer reported success, and no component raised an exception or logged an error. A single contaminated slot derails an entire generation, because attention reads every position.

blocks.text: The failure takes four steps:

inlines.text: A client disconnect, an admission rejection, or a transfer fault aborts request A mid-transfer while at least one launched write has not yet landed.
Decode frees A’s KVCache slots at abort time. The allocator marks them free while the remote writer is still writing to them.
The allocator hands those slots to victim request B.
A’s launched writes land inside B’s KVCache, and B decodes on foreign keys and values with no error.

blocks.text: These steps apply to any PD implementation that moves KVCache between engines with asynchronous DMA, push or pull, because each one has to decide when a slot is free. We diagnosed and fixed the family in SGLang.

blocks.text: Four facts about the system make each step possible.

blocks.text: 1. The allocator can mark a slot free while writes to it are in flight. In PD disaggregation, the decode engine pre-reserves destination KVCache slots for each incoming request, and its allocator tracks them as allocated or free. But “free” has a second, hidden condition: A slot is safe to reuse only when no remote writer can still touch it. The bugs in this class come from the gap between these two definitions. Each one is a distributed use-after-free, where the dangling pointer is a write request sitting in a NIC queue on another machine. The fix makes the second condition explicit, observable, and bounded.

blocks.text: 2. Launched RDMA work cannot be cancelled, for push and pull alike. SGLang’s KVCache transfer is push-based [3]. Prefill writes KVCache into decode’s memory, because prefill knows the moment it produces each chunk and can overlap transfer with ongoing computation, chunk by chunk. At and below the NIC, cancellation is hard to achieve without hurting availability. The RDMA API has no call that cancels an individual work request already posted to the NIC’s queue pair. Python cannot interrupt the transfer engine’s blocking C++ call (e.g., Mooncake’s batch_transfer_sync) mid-call. If that call times out, its work requests stay posted with no completion accounting, so those writes may land at an unknown later time. One-sided RDMA WRITE bypasses the receiver’s CPU, so decode gets no signal for each write that it could wait on. The NIC also places data per packet: A write interrupted mid-flight still leaves a partially written prefix at the destination, so even the paths that look like cancellation can mutate destination memory.

Freed-then-reassigned slots corrupt the transfer at either end.

blocks.text: 3. Complete liveness handling starts at the router but cannot end there. An abort is only safe when both halves of a P/D pair learn about it. A well-designed PD router cancels the pair together, so neither side waits out a 300-second timeout for a peer that is never coming. In sgl-router, #41612 builds the PD pairing on top of the abort-on-disconnect of #39461. The pair shares one router-minted request id. A client disconnect aborts decode, a prefill failure drops the decode request so the engine aborts it, and prefill learns of the abort through decode’s engine-side ABORT notification. sgl-model-gateway pairs the same two events (#19524 for disconnects, #29017 for prefill failures). Before that engine-side notification existed, a router that aborted only one side guaranteed the race: Decode released its slots while prefill, never told, kept pushing. Even a perfect router only narrows the window. The abort reaches prefill asynchronously, after some scheduling and network delay, and whatever the transfer engine already launched (an in-flight C++ call, posted work requests) continues regardless. The router decides who dies (abort orchestration), and the engine decides when memory is safe (drain correctness).

blocks.text: 4. The race window scales with prefill context length. SGLang chunks transfers and overlaps them with prefill computation, so the exposure window spans much of the prefill itself. A short prompt is in flight for milliseconds. A 128K–1M-token context, at tens to hundreds of kilobytes of KVCache per token depending on the model, keeps writes in flight for seconds to minutes, across many chunks and many posted work requests. The tail after the abort grows with it. A long context means more chunks in flight and more work requests still draining at the moment the abort lands, so launched writes can keep landing well after the allocator has reclaimed the freed slots. Under memory pressure, aborting a long request makes a write-after-reuse the expected outcome. Long-context workloads are also the ones where clients time out and disconnect mid-request. Long contexts therefore widen the window, lengthen the post-abort tail, and raise the abort rate all at once, so this bug class surfaces as deployments move to long-context serving.

PD disaggregation is enabled with a KVCache transfer backend (Mooncake, NIXL, MORI, or a custom

A request terminates mid-transfer (client disconnect, router cancel, timeout, transport fault, prefill failure, or hicache restore failure) while at least one of its writes is launched and not yet landed.

blocks.text: Deterministic or probabilistic? In production the race is probabilistic, so operators saw occasional corrupted outputs that they could not reproduce. Once the window is held open, it reproduces on demand (our harness in the next section, and the community reproducer in #32564). A client can raise the odds on purpose by sending long-context requests and disconnecting mid-transfer, which maximizes the race window and abort rate. The client cannot choose the victim or the landing slots, and the flow runs one way. The aborted request’s KVCache lands in another request’s KVCache, and nothing flows back to the aborter. The realistic impact is therefore one-way cross-request leakage, in which fragments of the aborted request’s context can surface in another client’s output, as they did in our reproduction. The aborter learns nothing, but in multi-tenant serving this is a data-leakage concern as well as an integrity one.

blocks.text: Failed Mooncake Sends

#43719, merged on October 12, 2026, closes an early-release path in the Mooncake drain ack. Before it, if a submitted Mooncake send returned an error, prefill marked the room failed and still acked it as drained once decode’s ABORT arrived. An error from batch_transfer_sync does not mean the writes stopped: After a timeout, the slices keep retrying, and after a failed batch, other tasks can still be in flight. Decode freed the slots on that ack, and the leftover writes could land in another request’s KVCache. #43719 withholds the drain ack for any room whose KVCache, state, or aux send failed, so decode holds the slots until its release timeout. Every failed send now costs that hold, until Mooncake can report whether a failed batch has drained. #43719 is on main, for release in v0.5.22.

blocks.text: Admission Fix

Admission control starts at the router. A PD router sends each request to a prefill worker and a decode worker together, and decode cannot produce a token without prefill’s KVCache. If prefill rejected or failed a request, the decode half used to wait out its 300-second timeout while it held a decode slot, so a burst of prefill failures could pin many decode slots at once. #29017 in sgl-model-gateway and #41612 in sgl-router now drop the decode request as soon as prefill returns an error, and the decode engine aborts it within seconds.

Two settings guard a Mooncake transfer call. The first is Mooncake’s own MC_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT (30 seconds by default), which fails any batch_transfer_sync call that takes longer. A call that fails this way can still leave writes in flight (fact 2), which is why prefill withholds the drain ack after a failed send.

blocks.text: The second is SGLANG_MOONCAKE_MAX_TRANSFER_BATCH_INDICES, added in #32758 (merged September 8, 2026), which caps the data volume, and with it the duration, of each call. At its default of 0, SGLang sends a chunk’s whole KVCache in one call, the efficient path. A positive value splits the transfer into ordered calls of at most that many indices, so a hung call strands at most one batch of posted writes, and the first failed call ends the loop before the remaining batches post. Smaller batches cost throughput and TTFT, so lower the limit only as an extra safeguard for extreme context lengths. In #32758’s tests, a single call for an 800K-token request carried 30 GB.

blocks.text: PD Checksum

#39500, merged on September 16, 2026, adds an optional integrity check for the transferred KVCache, off by default. Prefill computes an Adler-32 checksum on the GPU, over contiguous regions and over indexed KVCache and state pages, and sends it with the final chunk. Decode records it when it commits the transfer and checks the received KVCache against it before the request joins a running batch, so it catches late writes that land before that point; the hold keeps later writes out of reused slots. Decode keeps the checksum across retraction. A mismatch aborts the request and increments the transfer-failure counter; in CI, a mismatch raises an error instead. Health-check requests skip the check.

The drain ack often failed to arrive, so releases fell back to the timeout. A fault that decode did not itself initiate never armed the hold, which reopened the original bug by another path. We closed both on main between September 22 and 28, 2026: The hold now arms on every failure kind, and the drain ack now reaches decode. The audit also flagged prefill’s own source pages, and our analysis showed that path was already safe, because those bytes can only land in slots the decode hold is quarantining. #43562, merged on October 11, 2026, fixes a further finding, a rank-divergent HiCache restore.
